root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `g_date_set_parse()` may route the parser input into `g_utf8_casefold (str, -1)`, it must prove the source string is valid UTF-8 with `g_utf8_validate (str, -1, NULL)`. The vulnerable original violates that obligation on the stock `0xfd` witness while still reaching the casefold call; the fixed original guards that protected event away on the same witness, and the closest genuine witness is `valid_single_byte_boundary_0x7f`, where the protected casefold call executes with the guard satisfied.
root_cause_criterion.description: The missing root obligation is the absent UTF-8 validation guard in `g_date_set_parse()` before the date parser is allowed to treat the caller-provided NUL-terminated buffer as UTF-8.

nodes.state: At the sanitizer sink, the loop condition dereferences the same iterator pointer as `*p` in `while ((len < 0 || p < str + len) && *p)` immediately after the advancing `g_utf8_next_char()` step.
The month-name fallback reaches `g_utf8_casefold (str, -1)` with the same parser input pointer that `g_date_set_parse()` admitted, so the original buffer is consumed as UTF-8.
At the first iterator update inside `g_utf8_casefold()`, the local iterator `p` still aliases the same string address that the caller passed as `str`.
At the violating iterator step, `g_utf8_next_char (p)` changes the local iterator `p` from the original input address to a later address before the next loop-condition dereference.

edges.relation: The same parser-input pointer that should have been rejected by `g_utf8_validate (str, -1, NULL)` is later forwarded unchanged into `g_utf8_casefold (str, -1)`.
The `str` pointer passed into `g_utf8_casefold()` becomes the local iterator `p` at the first `g_utf8_next_char()` update.
The exact iterator value produced by `g_utf8_next_char (p)` is the same pointer the next loop-condition reevaluation dereferences as `*p` at the sanitizer sink.
